title: Enlarging a solution modulo q^n to contain a power of a unit
statement: Let $k$, $\Lambda$, $\mathfrak q$, $n$, $\varphi:k[y_1,\dots,y_m]\to\Lambda$, $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, $P=k[y_1,\dots,y_m]_{\mathfrak p}$ and $P/\mathfrak p^nP\to D\to\bar\Lambda:=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ be as in the conclusion of [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-solution-modulo]: $k$ a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\Lambda$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak p\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, $P\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and $P/\mathfrak p^nP\to D\to\bar\Lambda$ local homomorphisms of local Artinian rings with the first essentially smooth [def-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-ring-map] and the second flat. Then for every $\lambda\in\Lambda\setminus\mathfrak q$ there are an integer $q>0$ and a factorization $D\to D'\to\bar\Lambda$ of $D\to\bar\Lambda$ by local homomorphisms of local Artinian rings such that $D\to D'$ is essentially smooth, $D'\to\bar\Lambda$ is flat, and the image of $\lambda^q$ in $\bar\Lambda$ lies in the image of $D'$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07FI (lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo, line 2624), Section 07FF

proof.text: Put $S=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}/(\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q})^n$ and $x$ equal to the image of $\lambda$. The given hypotheses make $D$ and $S$ local Artinian rings and $g:D\to S$ flat and local. The injective $k\to S$ makes $S$ have characteristic $p$. Its residue field $K$ also has characteristic $p$, and the embedding $F=D/\mathfrak m_D\to K$ makes $F$ have characteristic $p$. Since $k$ is a field and $p>0$, $p$ is prime. Split into algebraic and transcendental cases for $\operatorname{res}_S(x)$ over $F$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Tag 07FI (lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo), lines 2642–2675

proof.text: In the algebraic case, apply separable-first/purely-inseparable to the finite simple extension $F(\operatorname{res}_S(x))/F$. Some $p$-power $p^e$ makes $b=\operatorname{res}_S(x)^{p^e}$ separable over $F$. In Lean this is proved using the separable closure of the simple intermediate field and then mapping back into $K$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Tag 07FI (lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo), lines 2642–2675

proof.text: Apply the separable residue-lifting lemma to $b$, obtaining finite étale local Artinian $D_1$ and a flat local map $g_1:D_1\to S$ factoring $g$, with $\operatorname{res}_S(g_1(d))=b$ for some $d$. Étale implies smooth; smooth implies essentially smooth by taking the algebra itself as the smooth presentation and localizing at $\{1\}$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Tag 07FI (lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo), lines 2642–2675

proof.text: The difference $g_1(d)-x^{p^e}$ lies in $\mathfrak m_S$. Choose $N$ with $\mathfrak m_S^N=0$. Since $p$ is prime, $p\ge2$ and $p^N\ge N$. Thus $(g_1(d)-x^{p^e})^{p^N}=0$. Frobenius gives $g_1(d)^{p^N}=(x^{p^e})^{p^N}$. Set $r=p^e p^N>0$ and use $d^{p^N}$ as the preimage of $x^r$. Ring homomorphisms commute with powers, so $x^r$ is exactly the displayed image of $\lambda^r$ in the original theorem.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Tag 07FI (lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo), lines 2642–2675

proof.text: In the transcendental case use the concrete polynomial localization lemma. It supplies an Artinian local essentially smooth factorization with $x$ itself in the image. Take $r=1$ and simplify $\lambda^1=\lambda$. These two cases prove the unchanged statement. No basis-lifting lemma or identification of $D[x]$ with $D[t]$ is used.
